dispatch.summary: T520 meets its acceptance, and I'm approving it. The diff is 592 lines, which is what flagged it as risky; I reviewed all of it. The publisher now compares values structurally with `sameJson` instead of comparing JSON text. It keeps one parsed copy of each large part, owned by a single published view: the copy is handed over when the part's text is unchanged, patched in place from the patch's own parsed JSON, and dropped when a key is added to an object. A base whose copy is already gone, such as an older base or the second diff on the same base, is parsed from its text again. The worker posts the patches as the `patchText` already written to size them, through `forPosting`. That works because the host spreads the publisher's `viewDelta` object into the reply unchanged, and replayed acknowledgments reuse the same object, so the lookup still finds the text. `applyViewDelta` reads `patchText` back, including `{}` for a value JSON leaves out. The client shares references only when the delta's base is its current view, and `store.publish` still re-shares afterwards, so the store's references and the `world` object's identity are kept. The 49-day test compares every delta byte for byte with an inline copy of the old publisher, including an older base every seventh day. Integration tests (`client.test.ts`, `host.test.ts`) and the full suite are left to the coordinator's final gate, as the task's result notes.

findings.message: The parsed copy is only dropped when a patch adds a key. A pure key reorder at a container level (an array, or a club object one level down) produces no patch entry, so the patched copy keeps the old key order while the new text has the new order. If two of the reordered keys are later removed together, the `d` list comes out in a different order than the previous publisher's. The rebuilt view is still the same, so this is harmless, but strictly it breaks byte-identical deltas. Optional fix: also drop the copy when the part's text changed but the patch has no entry for an object whose key order differs. Or just record this as a known limit.

Under ARCH-6 a worker failure restores the last checkpoint, so this is acceptable, but treating a throw from `collect` as `undefined` (engine computes the jobs) would match the 'failed helper' semantics completeRound already has. Leave it to T519 or document it.

Between prepareRound and completeRound only day and round stepping (beginDays) throw. T519's host must queue every command and checkpoint across that gap; consider an exported `roundPending(w)` so the host and checkpoint code can assert it.

reviewHistory.summary: T518 meets its acceptance and ARCH-6 r24, so I'm approving it. The risk flag was only about size (406 lines over 4 files). Most of that is the new round-jobs.ts module and its test; the season.ts change is a focused rewrite of the round step. `playRound` now runs in two phases: it computes every fixture first, then records them in fixture order. The record loop is unchanged from the old code. Before anything is recorded, each simulator result is matched back to the world's own squads, so recording one fixture can't change the roster used for another. If a result doesn't match its fixture, or names a player the world's squads don't have, the engine computes that fixture itself. A round that names a club twice still uses the old interleaved loop. The simulator is called only on a league day that includes our fixture, and our match plays on the engine meanwhile. Cup and continental days are unchanged. `prepareRound`/`completeRound` give T519 a synchronous split point. `beginDays` blocks day and round stepping while a round is pending, and `prepareRound` changes nothing when it returns false. I checked that `squad()`/`continuousSquad` read only `people`, `seed`, `year` and `playerClub` for NPC clubs, so own players out on loan don't pull `players` into the copy. The NPC squad cache is keyed per world, so a copy rebuilds its own squads as the impl notes intend. The three tests match acceptance (a)–(c). Test (a) also covers the prepare/complete pair and a helper failure, and checks the copy's keys. The worker reports matching day-bench hashes, with and without the simulator, at 49 and 301 days. findings.message: `completeRound` says a missing or unusable result is computed here, but a results array with a null entry crashes on `result.record.id`. A null entry is what a sparse array becomes after a JSON or worker round trip. Only true holes are skipped by `forEach`. Suggest skipping null entries, e.g. `if (!result) return`, so a partial helper failure from T519 falls back instead of throwing mid-round.

`w.calendar`/`w.round++` change before `start` runs. If `start` throws (for example a postMessage clone error in T519's host), the world is left mid-day with no pending entry, and the next `advanceDays` would skip that round's fixtures. ARCH-6's checkpoint restore covers this, but T519 should either guard `start` or restore the checkpoint on that error. Note it for T519.

Item 6 is checked [v], but the result's limits say the integration run (season.test.ts, world.test.ts, calendar.fast-path.test.ts) was not done. The coordinator's verify command (unit + contract) does not cover it either. The batch gate must run those integration files before T518 counts as done.

The unit test takes 7–12 s warm and 16.6 s cold. In the same parallel run, another file timed out at 37 s against the 30 s limit. Consider an explicit per-test timeout, or a shorter day count that still covers at least two own match days, so the unit gate doesn't fail intermittently under load.

While a round is pending, the beginDays guard makes advanceDays and advanceRound throw. I checked the independence argument against recordMatch: it writes only the two clubs' tables, Elo, bans and injuries, the NPC season stats, and own-only effects. NPC squad caches are invalidated only during club business, never inside a round. jobPlayback maps result IDs back to the world's squads and computes on the engine instead when a result doesn't match. The new tests cover acceptance (a) to (c): a reversed, JSON-round-tripped helper, plus the prepare pair and a failed helper, gives the same world over 60 days; a Proxy trace shows no key read outside FIXTURE_READ_KEYS and no writes; a duplicated club takes the fallback. findings.message: prepareRound is not exception-safe. beginRound advances w.round (and prepareRound sets w.calendar) before it calls `start` and plays our match, and pendingRounds is set only afterwards. If `start` throws (for example a postMessage DataCloneError in T519's host) or our match throws, the world is left half-stepped: the round counter has moved on, the round's fixtures are unscored, and nothing is pending. The host then cannot fall back to the engine-only path that ARCH-6 requires and can only restore the checkpoint. Consider registering the pending phase before calling `start`, or catching and rolling back, or at least documenting that T519 must treat a throw here as a checkpoint restore.

jobPlayback checks only the fixture ID, the two clubs and that every roster ID exists. A malformed helper result is not caught: a null entry, a missing `squads` (`?? []` turns it into an empty roster), or roster lines that don't cover the record's lineCounts. These would throw later inside recordMatch/settleNpcSeason after some fixtures are already recorded. The helpers are same-bundle code, so this is low risk, but either have T519's host validate results at the worker boundary (ARCH-6 'validated payloads') or treat a structurally incomplete result as unusable here, so the engine computes it instead.

Test (a) caches its no-simulator reference, which itself runs the new two-phase path. The suite therefore never compares against the old interleaved order; that identity rests only on the worker's manual day-bench hashes recorded in the task result. That is acceptable for the acceptance as written. A small committed regression would be cheaper to keep honest: for example, the interleaved loop inlined in the test over a few rounds, or the bench hash pinned for a tiny world.

Every failure path settles the round with `undefined` and never throws into prepareRound: an error reply, a short reply, a timeout, an unserializable copy, a throwing port, or `helpers-failed` from the client. Reads that arrive mid-day are held by `afterRound`, which re-checks `this.round` after every wakeup and so never observes a pending world; this was T518's stated hand-off. On the client, helpers are created only when hardwareConcurrency >= minCores (an undefined count is excluded) and their ports are handed over the same way as the codec's. A creation throw sends nothing and a helper onerror terminates them all. findings.message: ARCH-6 says both paths are 'checked by a test comparing a season played each way'. T519 compares worlds only through the first own match day: one helper round. T518's round-jobs.test.ts covers 60 days with an in-process simulator. Neither test covers a full season, and none runs the real HelperPool plus fixtureHelper path over several own match days. Consider adding a longer helper-path equality test in the integration tier (for example, several own match days, or a season on the pruned fixture world), or have the SSOT owner confirm that the 60-day plus first-match combination meets the clause.

When the engine-side pool disables itself after an error reply, a short reply or a timeout, the client is never told. Its helper Workers stay alive and idle, each holding a loaded engine module, until dispose(). Only a Worker onerror terminates them. This is optional: the engine worker could post a `helpers-off` notice so the client can terminate them, or the leftover workers can be accepted and documented.

Manual mode's `next-event` and the legacy `advance`/`season` commands still play own match days sequentially, as the result limits state. Auto-play (`advance-days`) and watched `next-match` do use the helpers, which covers this group's goal. If manual next-event should also gain the speedup, it needs a follow-up task with an engine change to nextEventDays.

- viewPublisher.ts: 값 하나하나를 JSON 문자열로 바꾸지 않고 구조로 비교합니다(`sameJson`). 큰 부분은 파싱해 둔 사본을 그 뷰 하나가 소유하고, 패치를 그 자리에 적용해 다음 비교에 다시 씁니다. 기준 텍스트를 매일 다시 파싱하지 않고, 사본이 없을 때만 파싱합니다. `forPosting`은 패치 크기를 잴 때 이미 만든 JSON 문자열(`patchText`)을 보냅니다.
- worker.ts: 응답을 `forPosting`을 거쳐 보냅니다.
- protocol.ts: `applyViewDelta`가 `patchText`를 읽고, 참조를 공유하는 함수(`ShareValue`)를 선택적으로 받습니다.
- client.ts: 지금 보고 있는 뷰 위에 델타를 적용할 때 store.ts에서 export한 `shareValue`로 참조를 그 자리에서 공유하고, 두 번째 `shareView` 순회는 건너뜁니다.

프로토타입에서 하나를 고쳤습니다. 패치가 객체에 새 키를 더하면 그 키가 다른 키들 사이 어디에 놓이는지 알 수 없습니다. 그래서 그 경우엔 파싱 사본을 보관하지 않습니다. 이 보호가 없으면 나중에 키 두 개를 지울 때 `d` 순서가 이전 퍼블리셔와 달라져 바이트가 어긋납니다. 이 보호를 일부러 끄면 49일 테스트가 실패하는 것도 확인했습니다.

실제로 돌린 검사(모두 통과):
- `pnpm run typecheck`, `pnpm run lint`, `pnpm run format:check`
- `vitest --project unit`: viewPublisher, protocol, store 테스트 (3개 파일, 30개 테스트)
- `vitest --project unit --project contract --changed 977f2571` (18개 파일, 199개 테스트)

돌리지 않은 것:
- 통합 테스트 `client.test.ts`, `host.test.ts`와 브라우저 테스트는 마지막 일괄 검증(배치)에서 돌리도록 결과 한계(limits)에 적었습니다.

review.summary: T516 removes the match-day moment completely. MATCH_DAY_MOMENT_MS, matchMoment, momentTimer/momentStep/momentBefore, beginMoment/endMoment/clearMoment, the NEXT MATCH moment overlay, the bottom moment slot, their CSS and the homeVisible prop are all gone, and no references remain in apps or tests. tick() no longer waits on a moment, so the next day comes on the normal pace interval, or once the step still in flight lands. The result notice moved into a new announce(next, before), which runs when the own-fixture step's reply lands. It compares the latest own match record before and after the step, as momentBefore did, and shows only while the clock is running, the tab is visible and 경기 결과 알림 is on. It still clears after RESULT_NOTICE_MS, which keeps WEB-18's 'once our fixture's day is shown' rule. Stop and hidden behaviour still holds: stop() and dispose() clear the notice, and announce checks running and hidden when the step lands. Risk reasons checked first: (1) the 453 changed lines are mostly deletions (112+/361-). (2) The edits outside touches are justified and kept minimal. App.tsx drops homeVisible and the controller prop that ClubHub no longer reads, and ClubHub.test.ts drops the removed moment case. Without them the build would not typecheck, and the worker recorded this in the result limits. Removing the slot does not move the mode switch or the AUTO/MANUAL text: .modeGroup is still flex:1 and left-aligned, and the slot was its last child. The unit tests replace the moment cases with the two required cases: a step that lands early or late, and the notice with the preference on and off, at its exact land time and exact expiry. The manual next-event case now proves no notice appears. The worker reports typecheck, lint, format:check, the changed unit/contract tests (94 passed) and the build. The rewritten progression-settings e2e journey was not run, by design; it is left to the coordinator's final batch.

새 파일 `packages/engine/src/round-jobs.ts`에 다음을 넣었습니다.
- 다른 클럽 경기가 읽는 월드 키 목록 `FIXTURE_READ_KEYS`와, 그 키만 담은 읽기 전용 사본을 만드는 `readCopy`
- 라운드 작업 목록 `roundJobs`, 헬퍼가 실행할 순수 함수 `simulateRoundJob`
- 결과의 선수 ID를 월드의 선수단과 다시 잇는 `jobPlayback`(맞지 않는 결과는 엔진이 직접 다시 계산)
- 월드마다 따로 주입하는 `setRoundSimulator`(기본은 없음)

시뮬레이터는 우리 리그 경기가 있는 날에만 쓰입니다. 다른 경기를 넘겨 시작시키고, 그동안 엔진 스레드에서 우리 경기를 치른 뒤 결과를 받습니다. 결과가 `undefined`면 엔진이 직접 계산합니다. T519 호스트가 비동기로 기다릴 수 있도록 `prepareRound`/`completeRound` 한 쌍도 `season.ts`에서 공개했고, 이 둘 사이에서는 `advanceDays`/`advanceRound`가 오류를 냅니다.

**확인한 것**
- day bench(프로토타입 bench-b 이식본) 해시: 시뮬레이터 없이 `098fdcae5ada357b`, 역순 처리 + JSON 왕복 시뮬레이터로도 같은 값입니다.

- typecheck, lint, format:check 통과.
- `round-jobs.test.ts` 3개 통과: (a) 60일 동안 동기 시뮬레이터, prepare/complete 쌍, 헬퍼 실패를 섞어 돌려도 시뮬레이터 없는 경우와 월드가 같음, (b) Proxy 추적으로 목록 밖 키 읽기·쓰기 없음, (c) 클럽 중복 시 예전 방식으로 처리.

review.summary: T520 meets its acceptance, and I'm approving it. The diff is 592 lines, which is what flagged it as risky; I reviewed all of it. The publisher now compares values structurally with `sameJson` instead of comparing JSON text. It keeps one parsed copy of each large part, owned by a single published view: the copy is handed over when the part's text is unchanged, patched in place from the patch's own parsed JSON, and dropped when a key is added to an object. A base whose copy is already gone, such as an older base or the second diff on the same base, is parsed from its text again. The worker posts the patches as the `patchText` already written to size them, through `forPosting`. That works because the host spreads the publisher's `viewDelta` object into the reply unchanged, and replayed acknowledgments reuse the same object, so the lookup still finds the text. `applyViewDelta` reads `patchText` back, including `{}` for a value JSON leaves out. The client shares references only when the delta's base is its current view, and `store.publish` still re-shares afterwards, so the store's references and the `world` object's identity are kept. The 49-day test compares every delta byte for byte with an inline copy of the old publisher, including an older base every seventh day. Integration tests (`client.test.ts`, `host.test.ts`) and the full suite are left to the coordinator's final gate, as the task's result notes.

findings.message: The parsed copy is only dropped when a patch adds a key. A pure key reorder at a container level (an array, or a club object one level down) produces no patch entry, so the patched copy keeps the old key order while the new text has the new order. If two of the reordered keys are later removed together, the `d` list comes out in a different order than the previous publisher's. The rebuilt view is still the same, so this is harmless, but strictly it breaks byte-identical deltas. Optional fix: also drop the copy when the part's text changed but the patch has no entry for an object whose key order differs. Or just record this as a known limit.

review.summary: T518 meets its acceptance and ARCH-6 r24, so I'm approving it. The risk flag was only about size (406 lines over 4 files). Most of that is the new round-jobs.ts module and its test; the season.ts change is a focused rewrite of the round step. `playRound` now runs in two phases: it computes every fixture first, then records them in fixture order. The record loop is unchanged from the old code. Before anything is recorded, each simulator result is matched back to the world's own squads, so recording one fixture can't change the roster used for another. If a result doesn't match its fixture, or names a player the world's squads don't have, the engine computes that fixture itself. A round that names a club twice still uses the old interleaved loop. The simulator is called only on a league day that includes our fixture, and our match plays on the engine meanwhile. Cup and continental days are unchanged. `prepareRound`/`completeRound` give T519 a synchronous split point. `beginDays` blocks day and round stepping while a round is pending, and `prepareRound` changes nothing when it returns false. I checked that `squad()`/`continuousSquad` read only `people`, `seed`, `year` and `playerClub` for NPC clubs, so own players out on loan don't pull `players` into the copy. The NPC squad cache is keyed per world, so a copy rebuilds its own squads as the impl notes intend. The three tests match acceptance (a)–(c). Test (a) also covers the prepare/complete pair and a helper failure, and checks the copy's keys. The worker reports matching day-bench hashes, with and without the simulator, at 49 and 301 days. The commit merges cleanly onto b525a8df; the T517/T520 changes since its parent are in the grid engine and the web runtime, not season.ts. Not verified here: the integration tests (season/world/calendar.fast-path) were not run by the worker, and the coordinator's verify list does not include them, so they rest on the batch gate.

reviewHistory.summary: T516 removes the match-day moment completely. MATCH_DAY_MOMENT_MS, matchMoment, momentTimer/momentStep/momentBefore, beginMoment/endMoment/clearMoment, the NEXT MATCH moment overlay, the bottom moment slot, their CSS and the homeVisible prop are all gone, and no references remain in apps or tests. tick() no longer waits on a moment, so the next day comes on the normal pace interval, or once the step still in flight lands. The result notice moved into a new announce(next, before), which runs when the own-fixture step's reply lands. It compares the latest own match record before and after the step, as momentBefore did, and shows only while the clock is running, the tab is visible and 경기 결과 알림 is on. It still clears after RESULT_NOTICE_MS, which keeps WEB-18's 'once our fixture's day is shown' rule. Stop and hidden behaviour still holds: stop() and dispose() clear the notice, and announce checks running and hidden when the step lands. Risk reasons checked first: (1) the 453 changed lines are mostly deletions (112+/361-). (2) The edits outside touches are justified and kept minimal. App.tsx drops homeVisible and the controller prop that ClubHub no longer reads, and ClubHub.test.ts drops the removed moment case. Without them the build would not typecheck, and the worker recorded this in the result limits. Removing the slot does not move the mode switch or the AUTO/MANUAL text: .modeGroup is still flex:1 and left-aligned, and the slot was its last child. The unit tests replace the moment cases with the two required cases: a step that lands early or late, and the notice with the preference on and off, at its exact land time and exact expiry. The manual next-event case now proves no notice appears. The worker reports typecheck, lint, format:check, the changed unit/contract tests (94 passed) and the build. The rewritten progression-settings e2e journey was not run, by design; it is left to the coordinator's final batch.

findings.message: prepareRound is not exception-safe. beginRound advances w.round (and prepareRound sets w.calendar) before it calls `start` and plays our match, and pendingRounds is set only afterwards. If `start` throws (for example a postMessage DataCloneError in T519's host) or our match throws, the world is left half-stepped: the round counter has moved on, the round's fixtures are unscored, and nothing is pending. The host then cannot fall back to the engine-only path that ARCH-6 requires and can only restore the checkpoint. jobPlayback checks only the fixture ID, the two clubs and that every roster ID exists. A malformed helper result is not caught: a null entry, a missing `squads` (`?? []` turns it into an empty roster), or roster lines that don't cover the record's lineCounts. These would throw later inside recordMatch/settleNpcSeason after some fixtures are already recorded. The helpers are same-bundle code, so this is low risk, but either have T519's host validate results at the worker boundary (ARCH-6 'validated payloads') or treat a structurally incomplete result as unusable here, so the engine computes it instead.

Test (a) caches its no-simulator reference, which itself runs the new two-phase path. The suite therefore never compares against the old interleaved order; that identity rests only on the worker's manual day-bench hashes recorded in the task result. That is acceptable for the acceptance as written. A small committed regression would be cheaper to keep honest: for example, the interleaved loop inlined in the test over a few rounds, or the bench hash pinned for a tiny world.

reviewHistory.summary: T518 meets its acceptance and ARCH-6 r24, so I'm approving it. The risk flag was only about size (406 lines over 4 files). Most of that is the new round-jobs.ts module and its test; the season.ts change is a focused rewrite of the round step. `playRound` now runs in two phases: it computes every fixture first, then records them in fixture order. The record loop is unchanged from the old code. Before anything is recorded, each simulator result is matched back to the world's own squads, so recording one fixture can't change the roster used for another. If a result doesn't match its fixture, or names a player the world's squads don't have, the engine computes that fixture itself. A round that names a club twice still uses the old interleaved loop. The simulator is called only on a league day that includes our fixture, and our match plays on the engine meanwhile. Cup and continental days are unchanged. `prepareRound`/`completeRound` give T519 a synchronous split point. `beginDays` blocks day and round stepping while a round is pending, and `prepareRound` changes nothing when it returns false. I checked that `squad()`/`continuousSquad` read only `people`, `seed`, `year` and `playerClub` for NPC clubs, so own players out on loan don't pull `players` into the copy. The NPC squad cache is keyed per world, so a copy rebuilds its own squads as the impl notes intend. The three tests match acceptance (a)–(c). Test (a) also covers the prepare/complete pair and a helper failure, and checks the copy's keys. The worker reports matching day-bench hashes, with and without the simulator, at 49 and 301 days. The commit merges cleanly onto b525a8df; the T517/T520 changes since its parent are in the grid engine and the web runtime, not season.ts. Not verified here: the integration tests (season/world/calendar.fast-path) were not run by the worker, and the coordinator's verify list does not include them, so they rest on the batch gate.

review.summary: T516 (rework submission 7dbbc96c on base 2de6ccc5): the rework is only a merge of work/auto-play into the original 3a33dfbb. git diff 3a33dfbb..7dbbc96c leaves progression.ts, every ui file and the e2e spec unchanged. The earlier integration failure was a 30 s timeout in the unrelated packages/engine/src/staff.hiring.test.ts, and the coordinator reports the rerun passes. The diff against 2de6ccc5 contains only T516 changes, so it does not collide with T517/T518/T520. I checked the risk reasons first. (1) The 453 changed lines are mostly deletions (112+/361-). (2) The App.tsx and ClubHub.test.ts edits outside touches are the minimum needed once the homeVisible/controller/moment props are gone, and the result limits record them. (3) The rework itself is a no-op merge. Acceptance holds. MATCH_DAY_MOMENT_MS, matchMoment, momentTimer/momentStep/momentBefore and beginMoment/endMoment/clearMoment are removed, and tick() no longer waits on a moment. Of the old names, the code and tests keep only the literal 'match-moment' and 'matchMoment' strings, which the new tests use to check they are absent. The result notice moved into announce(next, before), called after a visible, non-catch-up own-fixture step's reply is accepted. It runs after the cancel, critical, world-change and fresh-stop guards, so the old stop/eve/hidden outcomes are kept. It compares the latest own match record before and after the step, as momentBefore did, gates on running, !hidden and resultNotice, and clears after RESULT_NOTICE_MS. stop() and dispose() still clear it. The NEXT MATCH overlay, the bottom moment slot and their CSS are removed. The slot was the last child of the left-aligned mode group, so nothing else moves. The unit tests cover the two required cases with exact timing: the next step one pace interval after an early (50 ms) or slow (2500 ms) step lands, and the notice on/off at landing and expiry. They also cover stop and hidden with no notice, and manual next-event with no notice. ProgressControls.test.ts checks that neither mode has a slot. This matches the WEB@160 SSOT for WEB-18: no match-day pause or animation, and the notice once our fixture's day is shown. The rewritten progression-settings e2e journey has not been run and is left to the coordinator's batch.

review.summary: T519 meets its acceptance criteria. Risk reasons first: the 665 lines are mostly tests. The two files outside touches (client.test.ts and host.test.ts) are the integration tests that acceptance 6 explicitly asks to update. HelperPool splits jobs into contiguous shares and serializes the read copy once per round, before our match mutates the world. Results come back in job order. Every failure path settles the round with `undefined` and never throws into prepareRound: an error reply, a short reply, a timeout, an unserializable copy, a throwing port, or `helpers-failed` from the client. The pool then stays disabled, so that round and later ones run on the engine. playDay mirrors stepDay's league branch: prepareRound and completeRound cover beginDays, then beginRound, playRound and clubDay, and every other day falls through to advanceDays(w,1). Host.day sits inside the serialized execute queue. Reads that arrive mid-day are held by `afterRound`, which re-checks `this.round` after every wakeup and so never observes a pending world; this was T518's stated hand-off. The reply is built as before. Cancel stays per-day. On the client, helpers are created only when hardwareConcurrency >= minCores (an undefined count is excluded) and their ports are handed over the same way as the codec's. A creation throw sends nothing and a helper onerror terminates them all. The default test navigator stub has no hardwareConcurrency, so existing client tests are unaffected. helperPool.ts imports engine code only as types, so the client entry does not load the engine. Unit tests cover fixture order, partial shares, error, timeout, stale id, short reply, mid-round disable and serialization/port failures. They also cover playDay ordering and the non-own-day path. World equality is tested in host.test.ts (integration) through the real fixtureHelper serve and through a failing helper, alongside T518's 60-day equality, consistent with the test-tier rule. The worker's bench shows the same world hash and ratios of 0.58 and 0.68, inside the prototype band. The integration tests were not run by the worker and are left to the coordinator gate. Only optional P3 notes remain.

findings.message: ARCH-6 says both paths are 'checked by a test comparing a season played each way'. T519 compares worlds only through the first own match day: one helper round. T518's round-jobs.test.ts covers 60 days with an in-process simulator. Neither test covers a full season, and none runs the real HelperPool plus fixtureHelper path over several own match days. Consider adding a longer helper-path equality test in the integration tier (for example, several own match days, or a season on the pruned fixture world), or have the SSOT owner confirm that the 60-day plus first-match combination meets the clause.

When the engine-side pool disables itself after an error reply, a short reply or a timeout, the client is never told. Its helper Workers stay alive and idle, each holding a loaded engine module, until dispose(). Only a Worker onerror terminates them. This is optional: the engine worker could post a `helpers-off` notice so the client can terminate them, or the leftover workers can be accepted and documented.

Manual mode's `next-event` and the legacy `advance`/`season` commands still play own match days sequentially, as the result limits state. Auto-play (`advance-days`) and watched `next-match` do use the helpers, which covers this group's goal. If manual next-event should also gain the speedup, it needs a follow-up task with an engine change to nextEventDays.
